correctness.rationale: For semiaxes \(a\ge b>0\), differentiation of the exact perimeter integral yields \(\partial_aP<4\). Therefore, for \(\lambda\ge4\), \(P(a,b)-\lambda a\le(2\pi-\lambda)b\), with equality exactly for \(a=b\). The centered \(b\)-disk and the lattice covering radius force \(b\le\rho(\Lambda)\), attained by deepest-hole disks. For \(\lambda<4\), lattice-free row strips contain ellipses with fixed \(b\) and \(a\to\infty\) and \(P\ge4a\); for \(\lambda>2\pi\), shrinking disks approach the nonattained supremum zero. The argument covers both boundary coefficients and all equality cases. A quadrature diagnostic passed but is not the proof.

value.rationale: The general coefficient-\(4\) lattice-free perimeter question motivates the natural class of Euclidean ellipses. The result supplies the exact best constant and all extremizers for the square lattice, extends the classification to every full-rank planar lattice through its intrinsic covering radius, and locates the two sharp phase thresholds \(4\) and \(2\pi\) for the entire perimeter–circumradius penalty family. This is a complete shape-class extremal classification and benchmark, not just a numerical improvement or parameter renaming.
